Perfume rating 4.08 out of 5 with 12,185 votes

La Nuit Trésor by Lancôme is a Oriental Vanilla fragrance for women. La Nuit Trésor was launched in 2015. La Nuit Trésor was created by Christophe Raynaud and Amandine Clerc-Marie. Top notes are Pear, Tangerine and Bergamot; middle notes are Strawberry, Vanilla Orchid, Black Rose and Passionfruit; base notes are Praline, Caramel, Vanilla, Litchi, Patchouli, Incense, Coffee, Licorice, Coumarin and Papyrus.

Lancome launches La Nuit Tresor fragrance in February 2015. The scent is a flanker of the original Tresor from 1990.

The composition is announced as a gourmand aphrodisiac and a love potion created by perfumers Christophe Raynaud and Amandine Marie. It supposedly depicts the dark side of rose and mixes notes of black rose with Tahitian vanilla orchid absolute. There are also accords of natural incense, papyrus, patchouli and litchi praline added to the mix.

The faces of the campaign are Penélope Cruz and Ilay Kurelović and photo signed by Mert Alas and Marcus Piggott. Video campaign directed by Rob Marshall.

The bottle is decorated with a diamond-shaped satin black rose and bow. The fragrance is available as 30, 50 and 100 ml Eau de Parfum.

herculano

Okay. I have the original formulation, now. Batch code checked.
(I also have the reformulation)

It took me years and patience to find an original formulation.

And right off the bat i can tell you two things:

Original is wayyyyy stronger, MUCH better projecting, and truly long lasting.

The other thing i can tell you is that the two versions DO smell very similar.

So when i first bought the modern La Nuit (several years ago) i was disappointed. I was kinda surprised to find it begin with rose drier sheets. Nice but soapy. Not what i was expecting. The dry down, however, was beautiful. There is a waxy/lipstick thing in the modern La Nuit that i find absolutely addicting and yummy.

However this whole experience was unforgivably short lived. No longevity. No projection.

I wanted an original formulation so bad.
But good luck finding one.
Needle in a hay stack.

Anyway, i finally stumbled across one, and let me tell you its a true BOMB.

Take the modern version and amp it, and deepen it. Also make it sweeter! And smokier. Literally everything is bigger or deeper.

Thats how the original comes across to me. There are supposedly more notes in the original but to me its simply a superior (intense/pure parfum) version of the more recent one.

As if the first formula was a pure Parfum, and the second version an EDT.

This one is an absolute stunner.

To be honest, it took me a minute to process this difference because its so incredibly strong its almost too much. And i love big powerful perfumes.

If you want it, just keep at it. It took me a long time to find it, but its doable.

Many sellers arent even aware of the reformulation, so you can get the old version for a good price with some luck.

Bunnyance

The fragrance is very different from what I expected. Firstly it is not as sweet as the notes suggest, as after the first boozy and fresh notes fades, all I can feel from afar is the patchouli but it is a nice one - juicy, sweet and fruity. Smelling up close I feel the coffee, licorice, caramel and vanilla.
It's not bad, in facts it is a good, well composed and warm fragrance but I'm bummed that after 10-15 min I only feel the patchouli, even if it is good. From all the listed notes and longevity I hoped there would be more spice and flavor in this but what I got is a fruitchuli which I don't want at the moment. I reapplied throughout the day but still nothing changes. Maybe my batch is not good but it definitely does not have strong or enormous sillage or lasting power, it turns very subtle after 2-3h.
Yes - if you want a not so sweet and strong fruitchuli
No - if you are looking for a sweet, spicy and syrupy fragrance (not like la vie est belle - not that sweet and syrupy)

Linissleepy 09/03/25 18:01

This is certainly a contender for one of my top fragrances I own out of about 200, it's more beautiful than I was hoping for. Put off buying it bc of the price tag for so long, and after finally biting the bullet during Lancomes last sale, it was worth every penny for a 100ml bottle. The performance is insanely good, great projection, and lasts for a good 6-8 hours for me, can still smell it the next morning if I wear it at night.

The fragrance itself is so gorgeous, starts out with a burst of tart fruitiness (assume litchi), and a bright rose. It progressively dries down to become a very "night-time" scent, the incense and caramel/praline combo is amazing. The rose turns a little ashy but overall remains the center and sits atop the deep sweetness in the base, would absolutely recommend for winter and fall, but definitely not for hotter weather or daytime. This fragrance is vampy, powerful, seductive, and extremely cvnt, so if you don't want people to notice you, skip it.

Sweet sweet raspberry sugary dream with a depth to it.

You have to be in the mood for this one but when you are, it hits the spot!

McKTea 05/08/25 10:40

So many hilarious reviews of this Trésor La Nuit, calling it "old." There are different needs and preferences at different stages of life, such as medicines, vitamins, entertainment, comforts, supports.

Age groupings for fragrances, however, are entirely a marketing strategy.

This isn't exactly my type of fragrance. It is strictly in the "like" or "decent" category for me. But I have the discovery set for Kayali, and let me tell you: This girl smells like a hybrid of trending Kayali blockbusters. She opens similar to Eden Sparkling Lychee, except a little less juicy and with that stronger anchoring floral musk note common in modern sweet fragrances circa 2013 to present, and the drydown is almost exactly like Vanilla Rock Candy Sugar.

There is a distinctly vintage cosmetics note to it, albeit a musky one. I get zero smokiness on my skin with the EDP, but I also used a light touch in applying it. People who find it "old" are likely used to EDTs or watered-down EDPs and are overspraying. You mustn't be greedy with her.

So with this, I detect cosmetics mélange with litchi and patchouli, and just a hint of coffee. At the time of her release, many may have considered her a sweet gourmand fragrance, but now that more photorealistic true gourmands have arisen, this is more of a fruity floral oriental, perhaps. Here it is classified as an "Oriental vanilla," but there is nothing vanilla about this fragrance. Not with that base, in any case.

She is more grounded than an ethereal violet composition, but less sweet and even more powdery. She is less flowery and fruity than Vera Wang Princess, less sweet than Aquolina Pink Sugar, less juicy and sparkling than Kayali Eden Sparkling Litchi, less vintage floral than Jardins d'Armide, less powdery feminine giggle than Keiko Mecheri's Loukhoum. She's closer to Vanilla Rock Candy Sugar to my reckoning. If she smells like Grandma, Grandma must have worn heavy designer makeup when she hugged or kissed you, and that's the scent you recall lingering in the base. Other than that, she feels modern. Maybe your big sister who raided Grandma's cosmetics bag and now is wearing Kayali with vintage lipstick, blush, and concealer.

femininehorror 03/11/24 17:29

This scent sparked my first love for perfume.
In my teen years, I remember sitting in an outdoor cafe in the heat of the Grecian summer. I had been visiting my family there for several weeks, and had managed up until that point to cope with the difficulties of not speaking the same language as most of my family members. I chatted casually with my father under the thin awning, not really to talk but to pass the time while the others at the table caught up on years of stories.
Our waitress strolled by, wafting with her the most intoxicating scent. My conversation with my father stopped abruptly. We could only look at each other with open-mouthed amazement. She. Smelled. SO GOOD!!
Cue ten minutes of us begging the rest of our family to ask her in Greek which perfume she was wearing. This is the only time in my life I have asked a stranger their perfume. She was wearing La Nuit Tresor.
Still to this day I wear it and remember that summer afternoon.

Also this is the only perfume I've worn and gotten fun comments from acquaintances like smelling delicious, yummy, and my favorite, "Someone in this room smells EXPENSIVE!"

Jade-Ange D 08/21/23 13:11

What a superbly good gourmand/fruity every day kind of fragrance.

I think that the olfactive pyramid of this fragrance was perfectly created :

• Top notes : You get your fresh fruits, helping for a bit of a lighter and brighter touch : Pear / Tangerine / Bergamot

• Middle Notes : It is now slightly floral, stays fruity but starts to get sweeter and yummy : Strawberry /Vanilla Orchid / Black Rose / Passionfruit

• Base Notes : Let the sweeeeeet gourmand heaven begin ! : Caramel / Litchi / Vanilla / Patchouli / Incense / Coffee / Licorice / Coumarin / Papyrus

But if I just try to find the prominent notes, I’ll say that the Caramel / Coffee / Strawberry / Passionfruit and Vanilla are the stars of the show.

I think that La Nuit Trésor isn’t my favorite from the line, La Nuit Trésor Intense is.
But it stays beautiful and I seem to love it.

The lasting power and sillage is insane, it is a powerhouse don’t spray too much or you’ll kill anyone around you by causing them a headache and/or nausea. It’s one of these perfumes that are forbidden to overspray.

I fell in love with that amazingly well blended scent. I am a sucker for Gourmand and Fruity perfumes, so La Nuit Trésor definitely got me good. 9/10 !

Oops, I missed the smokiness when I was testing it from a mini. I would dab it on my wrist when going to bed and fall asleep by the time it got around to fuming. Now, I’ve got the whole 75ml of it and I’m normally averse to smoky incense. Well, there’s the gemstone of a bottle to console me, right? (Wouldn’t that be a dream to amass all the dark bottles from the collection?) But even now that I’m awake to this normally objectionable facet, I’m still into this fragrance. It’s sweet, not bitter on me even when smoky. Addictive sweetness - if I am to sum up this blend - fruity and floral first and then gourmand sweetness. Being very rich, dense and potent, it needs to be applied sparingly. One spritz goes a long way, meaning I’ll never be able to finish my bottle.

PS: is this the most reviewed fragrance or what? My finger got numb from scrolling and still I could never reach the bottom.

Update: I’m struck by the resemblance between this and Fancy by Jessica Simpson. I’m comparing them side by side. Given than Fancy was released in 2008, that would make La Nuit a dupe.

Most Popular Positive Reviews

bolla2909 05/16/20 11:55

Let me paint you a little picture for this one.

It's a cold afternoon in December and you are getting ready for a night out. You take a long hot bath with your delicious smelling face mask and soak up the relaxing atmosphere. Afterwards you paint your nails a dark colour, while in your black satin and lace bathrobe. It's getting darker and all the Christmas lights give off a warm and cosy vibe. You put on your makeup and do your hair and choose a dress. It's a burgundy coloured satin dress, with a deep neckline and tied together at the waist. As it's a very cold night you put on black opaque tights as well and reach for your black lace up pointy toe high heeled boots.

You look in the mirror and think to yourself that you look just the right amount of witchy, sexy and seductive. But. You need to smell accordingly. You look over to your vanity. What would suit tonight and this look well? You need something deep, spicy, a little sweet and mysterious. Something that will shine in cold weather and is big enough to have you stand out in a crowd. But not something loud and brass. Something smooth but bold.

You pick up the beautiful diamond shaped bottle and instantly know that nothing else will do tonight. Sweet incense wrapped up in patchouli and praline, with delicious caramel and vanilla lending support on the side. And deep in the heart of it are dark and velvety roses. Sugary roses.

You spray it on and feel like the whole ensemble came together. You feel sexy and you are ready to go out and devour the night. You put on your velvety soft faux fur jacket, black leather gloves and and your bag, top up your lip gloss and run out the door. Outside the cold greets you but you are comfortably enveloped in your warm jacket and perfume. It starts to snow and the whole place becomes magical. Golden fairy lights, the smell of roasted almonds, people with their Christmas shopping and distant music. You smile and get smiles back. You feel good. You can't wait to get to the restaurant where you're meeting your girlfriends, to enjoy a dinner by the fireplace that will be filled with laughter, naughty stories and heavenly treats. You take a deep breath and smell the frost in the air mingled with La Nuit Tresor. Perfect, you think to yourself. Just perfect.

You step off the curb and walk into the crowd next to the Christmas tree. This will be a good night and you know it.

That was my little story. Thanks for reading.

mevans 09/03/19 10:21

The opening is like sleeping in and waking up to belgian waffles, syrup and coffee. It's sweet, decadent, and delicious. The caramel and vanilla are distinctly identifiable. The praline and litchi are supporting and accenting. The fruits, florals and coffee are all blended so well I can't pick them out specifically but it's not a caramel-vanilla linear scent so all are playing their part. La Nuit Tresor is a gourmand for gourmand lovers. It aims to turn you into a gourmand lover if you aren't one already. You have to give it a try to really understand how lovely this fragrance is. comfortablynumb83 01/20/18 03:21

I've been putting off writing a review for this one because there aren't enough words to describe just how beautiful this scent is. I had gotten a sample in a swap and as soon as i inhaled that first whiff, I was in love. I was instantly addicted and went on a witch hunt for a bottle and one of my favorite people here swapped me her bottle. :) 2 months ago I got the 1.7 oz from her and it was full. I'm already down to just 1/3 of a bottle and there is only that much left because I've been trying my hardest not to use it until I have another bottle! :)
Anyway, let's talk about this scent. It will hypnotize and seduce you, lure you in. Once you've smelled la nuit tresor there is no going back. If you aren't wearing la nuit then you are thinking about it. It's as addictive as any narcotic. It is sweet but this is not just "another sweet scent." I detected raspberry but saw it isn't listed here, however, if you go to Lancome's website raspberry is listed as one of the key notes, along with frankincense, which is what plays a part in making la nuit different from every other fruitchuli. This is incredibly sweet but the frankincense takes this from being a sweet fruit bomb (which I have no issues with!) To being a sultry, seductive goddess that deserves to be put on a pedestal. Be prepared to fall madly in love with la nuit!

Luxury Problem 06/18/17 12:13

Best blind buy ever! Gourmand and sweet but not remotely cloying. Sultry and dark without any dirty earthy patchouli notes. Pretty yet still sexy and intense. Unique but not weird or off-putting. Everything is perfectly balanced.

A rich dark gourmand fragrance primarily with a hint of exotic smoky incense floating in the background. This just may be my favorite perfume of all time! For purposes of comparison I have La Vie Est Belle on one wrist and La Nuit Tresor on the other and can guarantee you these two smell nothing alike. On one side, La Vie Est Belle is screechingly loud, demanding attention, while La Nuit Tresor is soft and sultry, whispering to come closer, wink. This one is pure sexiness bottled. I want to always smell like this.

ETA: This perfume is supposed to be an aphrodisiac and according to my fiancé, it's definitely working! He is a fragrance SNOB especially when it comes to sillage and longevity and he says La Nuit Tresor surpasses his strictest standards in that department. He has told me I smell amazing about 1000 times since I came home wearing this. He says he can smell me from across the room in the best way, and he wants me to add in my review that this perfume is so potent that he can smell it on himself after snuggling with me and he feels like he can smell me on him and he loves it! Signature fragrance found!

cocogirl96 05/07/20 20:44

After hearing many people say that Jessica Simpson Fancy is a cheap and juvenile version of La Nuit Tresor, I blind bought La Nuit Tresor. Jessica Simpson Fancy was my fav perfume growing up and I still love it. I expected La Nuit Tresor to replace it. To be a more grown version of it. I don't think Jessica Simpson Fancy is a dupe for this, nor do I think La Nuit Tresor is better than Jessica Simpson Fancy. I said all this to say: if you are thinking of buying this because people said it smells like a better version of Fancy, reconsider it. Don't blind buy it for those reasons, like I foolishly did. I will pick that $18 Fancy bottle over this $100+ bottle any day of the week.

With that said, I still like this scent. It's a very complex, rich, deep, and sweet scent. Very sexy and thoughtfully formulated. My biggest problem with it is the opening. The opening smells like a combination of incense, chocolate, and orange, which is really gross to me. Then it moves to likable fruity-floral scent with a hint of chocolate, but it's nothing interesting. After a few hours of wearing it, it leaves a sexy combination. I can't pinpoint the notes, but they work really well with my skin.

I wouldn't wear this perfume every day. This fragrance requires a very specific time to be worn. It must be during the dead middle of winter. It must be at night, and it can't be a formal event. It doesn't scream sophistication. More like a party scent, running close to the tacky category, but not quite there. It's too heavy to be worn any other way. Also, I would have to wear it for a few hours before I could actually enjoy the beauty of the scent because the opening is so terrible and the middle notes are mediocre. To me, it's not worth it.

Overall, I give it a 6 out of 10. I don't hate it, but if I could go back, I wouldn't have bought it.

WARNING - SCATHING REVIEW TO FOLLOW

FINALLY saw this in stores today. I am in the US and have been curious about it since the Fragrantica article on it came out. Guess it is exclusively at Dillards for now, if you are curious. I was so excited to see this perfume that I had been wondering about for months, that I picked up the bottle and lavishly applied 3 spritzes to my right arm.

SCRUBBER. I really hate this. I can see where people would enjoy it, but I can't stand it. The orchid is so disgusting and synthetic, there is some lichi in there reminding me of Hypnose [which oddly I really love], plus the now-typical patchouli bomb a la Calvin Klein Euphoria, but done badly. I do NOT get the LVEB similarity at all. Euphoria + a little bit of Angel is more what I am getting.

I don't know if cloying is the word to use, but this stuff is so heavy it almost felt like I was breathing in something semi-solid. I guess it DOES have that going for it, Lancôme always gets the projection part right ;). Anyway, this is not very popular where I live, and I am glad. If someone was wearing this around me I would hold my breath until they left.
